chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman from the Banu Umayya died, so I attended her (funeral). So when they had prayed over her, and raised her, and she came to be in the hands of the men, he said: 'O Allah! Place her down and do not raise her, and do not purify her.' He said, 'And she was an enemy of Allah.' He said, 'And (an enemy) of ours.'

key_terms.بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ: Banu Umayya (the clan of Umayya, known for their rivalry with the Prophet's family)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about the enemy of Allah during her funeral?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s specific supplication for a woman of the Banu Umayya, invoking divine placement and lack of purification to signify her enmity (Nasibi) towards the Ahl al-Bayt. Scholarly context emphasizes that this act serves as a practical demonstration of 'Tajrih' (disparagement) and 'Taqrib' (elevation) within Shia jurisprudence, illustrating how the Imams actively reinforced the theological status of their political and spiritual adversaries. The phrase 'and to us' (wa lana) further personalizes this enmity, linking the individual’s fate directly to the lineage of the Prophet and his Imams.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Al Hajjal, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A woman from the Clan of Umayya died, so I attended her (funeral). So when Salaat had been prayed over her, and she was raised, and came to be in the hands of the men (for the burial), heasws said: ‘O Allahazwj! Place her down and do not Raise her, and do not Purify her’. He (the narrator) said, ‘Amd she was an enemy of Allahazwj, and I do not know it except that heasws said: ‘And (an enemy of) oursasws’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah al-Hajjal from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from abu‘ Abd Allah or from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Once a woman of banu ‘Umayyah died and I was present in her funeral. When they performed Salah (prayer) and picked her body when on the hands of men he (the Imam) said, ‘O Lord, put her down and do not raise her and do not cleanse her.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘She was an enemy of Allah -I think he said- and our (enemy).”’
